brief:
Israel's political establishment is reassessing its strategy after US voters rejected Donald Trump, the Israeli prime minister's preferred candidate, according to Al Jazeera English. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had wagered significantly on a Trump victory, banking on continued US support for Israeli military operations in Gaza and the broader Middle East.

The electoral outcome now forces Israeli leadership to confront both Trump's defeat and its own role in damaging bilateral relations. Analysts suggest Netanyahu's positioning on the Trump alliance may have contributed to deepening the political isolation Israel faces internationally, while simultaneously leaving the country without the expected backup from Washington.
dek: Israel's political establishment grapples with US voter rejection of White House ally and own contribution towards it.
title: Netanyahu's Trump gamble backfires as US voters reject White House ally
